name: Mandarin Chinese
notes: The most widely spoken first language in the world. Grammar is genuinely simple — no verb conjugation, no plurals, no tenses in the European sense. The difficulty is the four tones and the characters. Learn Pinyin with tone marks first; the tone is part of the word, not an accent, and mā, má, mǎ and mà are four different words.
syllabus: HSK 1, 2 and 3 in full — 600 words, the first three of nine official levels, about 620 cards. HSK 3 is everyday conversation: the past, comparisons, reasons, plans, feelings. Tones matter more than vocabulary at this stage: the guide explains them. Cards can be spoken aloud if Windows has a Chinese voice installed. Next would be HSK 4 (another 600 words).
